FOR CLAUDE CODE & CODEX

The work merged.
Clear the worktree.

Ten worktrees. Seven merged last week.
And a folder full of handoffs nobody reads.

Lumberjack checks what landed, removes eligible worktrees, and keeps their branches. Work documents go to trash after a grace period; research and unfinished work stay. A Stop gate keeps agents off misnamed branches.

01 / THE SWEEP

Landed work goes.
Unfinished work stays.

One repository, six worktrees and their work documents, over five weeks. Step through the sweeps: every row that changes is marked, and the log shows the sweep's real output.

      SESSION START, DAY 0WHAT THE SWEEP PRINTS

      The examples simulate a repository; nothing on your machine is read. Squash or rebase merge? The sweep proves it from git when the merged content matches, or from the exact tip of a merged PR with a logged-in gh. Patch similarity alone never removes anything.

      02 / STOP GATE

      Wrong branch?
      The turn doesn't end.

      When an agent tries to end its turn, the gate checks two things:

      • The branch is named <owner>/<ticket>-<slug>, as your settings define.
      • The primary checkout is still on main, with the work in a worktree.

      If either fails, the first Stop attempt is blocked with the reason and the fix. It blocks once per turn, so an agent never loops.

      TRY ITWHERE THE AGENT STOPS
      Stop attempt 1: allowed. The branch is well named and the work is in a worktree.

      03 / SETUP

      Setup asks.
      You commit.

      Run setup once per repository. It reads the repository, then asks about branch names, worktree roots, doc roots, cleanup and the Stop gate, each with a recommended answer. After your yes it writes your settings, a post-merge hook block (so a merge also sweeps), a block in CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md, and optionally .claude/settings.json so teammates get the plugin.

      It never commits. Review git diff and commit it yourself.

      INSTALL

      Put it to work.

      Install for your agent, run setup in the repository, then review and commit the changes. The next session start runs the sweep.

      REQUIREMENTS

      Git + Python 3.11 or newer.
      gh is optional, for pull-request evidence.

      Full installation guide ↗
      IN CLAUDE CODE, ONE AT A TIME
      1. /plugin marketplace add VforVal/lumberjack
      2. /plugin install lumberjack@lumberjack
      THEN, IN YOUR REPOSITORY

      Restart Claude Code, then run:

      /lumberjack:setup

      Answer the setup questions. Review git diff and commit the generated configuration.

      IN YOUR TERMINAL
      1. codex plugin marketplace add VforVal/lumberjack
      2. codex plugin add lumberjack@lumberjack
      THEN, IN CODEX

      Restart Codex. Run /hooks once to review and trust the plugin hooks, then choose lumberjack:setup from the skill picker. Review git diff and commit.

      Updating? Re-run setup after each plugin update, so it can ask about new settings. Standard-library Python; no runtime packages to install.

      Before enabling cleanup, see the plan with sweep_worktrees.py --preview.
